title: Stage 4: Ship OpsKit to the team
summary: Make OpsKit a module the team can install: a manifest, Pester tests, a clean PSScriptAnalyzer run, and version 1.0.0 on the team feed.

steps.title: Done means installable
body: Three functions on your disk help you. The same three functions on the team feed, with tests and a version,
help everyone, and can be updated safely. The release checklist the team uses:
1. a manifest that exports exactly the public functions, with a version, a description and the minimum PowerShell;
2. Pester tests that pass (and would fail if the code broke);
4. published to the feed; teammates run `Install-PSResource OpsKit -Repository TeamFeed`.

steps.explain: Tests and lint in either order, but both before anything leaves your machine. Publishing is the last step and is hard to take back: a version on a feed should never be replaced, only superseded.

steps.title: OpsKit 1.0.0
prompt: All three functions are in `~/src/OpsKit/Public/`. Release **OpsKit 1.0.0**:
`New-ExpenseReport` and `Rename-ScanByDate`, with an author, a description and PowerShell `7.4`;
2. **`~/src/OpsKit/tests/OpsKit.Tests.ps1`** with **at least 3** passing tests (use `TestDrive:` for files);
4. register `~/feed` as the trusted repository **`TeamFeed`** and **publish** OpsKit to it.

checks.name: the manifest
checks.fail: `Test-ModuleManifest ~/src/OpsKit/OpsKit.psd1` should show 1.0.0, the three functions, PowerShell 7.4, a description and an author.

checks.name: at least 3 tests, all passing
checks.fail: `Invoke-Pester ~/src/OpsKit/tests/OpsKit.Tests.ps1` should pass with at least 3 tests.

checks.name: PSScriptAnalyzer is clean
checks.fail: PSScriptAnalyzer still reports findings (listed). Fix the code, not the rules.

checks.name: OpsKit 1.0.0 is on TeamFeed
checks.cmd: ls ~/feed; pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -c 'Find-PSResource -Name OpsKit -Repository TeamFeed -ErrorAction Stop | ForEach-Object { "found $($_.Name) $($_.Version)" }'

hints: `New-ModuleManifest -Path ~/src/OpsKit/OpsKit.psd1 -RootModule OpsKit.psm1 -ModuleVersion 1.0.0 -FunctionsToExport Get-FolderUsage, New-ExpenseReport, Rename-ScanByDate -Author 'Ops team' -Description '...' -PowerShellVersion 7.4 -CmdletsToExport @() -VariablesToExport @() -AliasesToExport @()`. Without the last three, the template writes `'*'` and PSScriptAnalyzer flags it (`PSUseToExportFieldsInManifest`).

Tests: `BeforeAll { Import-Module "$PSScriptRoot/../OpsKit.psd1" -Force }`, then e.g. folders in `TestDrive:` for Get-FolderUsage, a PDF with a set `LastWriteTime` for Rename-ScanByDate (and one with `-WhatIf`), a small CSV for New-ExpenseReport. `TestDrive:` is shared by every test in a `Describe`: clean up in `BeforeEach` when a test changes files.
solution: New-ModuleManifest -Path ~/src/OpsKit/OpsKit.psd1 -RootModule OpsKit.psm1 -ModuleVersion 1.0.0 -FunctionsToExport Get-FolderUsage, New-ExpenseReport, Rename-ScanByDate -Author 'Ops team' -Description 'Daily ops chores: share usage, scanner inbox, expense reports.' -PowerShellVersion 7.4 -CmdletsToExport @() -VariablesToExport @() -AliasesToExport @()
explain: That is the whole loop a PowerShell team runs: code in a repo, tests and lint as the gate, a versioned package on a
feed, `Install-PSResource` on every machine. Next steps you could take at work: a CI pipeline that runs stages 2 and
3 of the checklist on every pull request, `Update-ModuleManifest -ModuleVersion 1.1.0` plus a changelog for each
release, and a scheduled task (module 8) that runs `Get-FolderUsage` every night.
